_comment: Manifest for the self-hosted Alaska lidar DEM collection.
target_epsg: the *appropriate local UTM zone*, NAD83(2011) realization.
MatSu is delivered tagged UTM 5N but spans 150.5W - 147.0W, i.e. almost
entirely zone 6 and up to 3 degrees past the zone 5 edge. It is the one
dataset that gets a genuine zone change.
Source datum tags are honored literally (user decision, 2026-09-05):
Lower_KP and MatSu declare WGS 84, so a real WGS84 -> NAD83(2011) datum
transform is applied to them. Homer (NAD83) and KBay (NAD83(2011)) stay
in the NAD83 family. If the WGS84 tags turn out to be a vendor mislabel,
those two will sit ~1-2 m off Homer/KBay and must be rebuilt with an
max_zoom: chosen so one web-mercator pixel ~= one source pixel at that

datasets.title: Homer 2019 bare-earth DTM
datasets.notes: Source NAD83 / UTM 5N (EPSG:26905), LZW, 128x128 blocks. No vertical CRS declared.

datasets.title: Lower Kenai Peninsula lidar DEM
datasets.notes: Source tagged WGS 84 / UTM 5N (EPSG:32605). Uncompressed and stripe-blocked (43603x1) - must be converted to a tiled COG before any windowed read. No vertical CRS declared.

datasets.title: Kachemak Bay 2023 lidar DEM
datasets.notes: Arrives as a valid COG (ZSTD, 512 blocks) in a COMPOUND CRS: NAD83(2011) / UTM 5N + NAVD88 height. Already the target horizontal zone, so the archive stage copies rather than warps - warping to a 2D EPSG:6334 would be an identity resample that also silently drops the declared NAVD88 vertical datum. It is the only one of the four that declares its vertical reference.

datasets.title: Mat-Su Valley 2019 bare-earth DEM
datasets.notes: 82 GB SAGA .sdat, stripe-blocked. No vertical CRS declared. ELEVATIONS ARE IN FEET and are converted to metres on ingest (vertical_scale): the raw grid reads 246.1 at Palmer and 341.5 at Wasilla, whose published elevations are 240 ft and 344 ft - a metres reading would put downtown Palmer at 807 ft. Homer and Lower Kenai agree with each other in metres at an overlap point (19.84 vs 20.06), so the foot units are MatSu's alone. International foot assumed; the US survey foot differs by 2 ppm (3 mm at 1500 m), which is far below the data's own accuracy. Zone-5-tagged but lies in zone 6 - this is the one real reprojection. max_zoom 16 (1.14 m) rather than 17 (0.57 m): 17 would oversample 0.91 m source 1.6x for 4x the bytes.

datasets.title: Matanuska Valley 2011 bare-earth DTM (9 ft)
datasets.notes: Mat-Su Borough 2011 lidar (flown 2011-05-10..12), Matanuska River corridor from Palmer east to ~147.2W. Source is NAD83 / Alaska State Plane zone 4 in US survey feet (FIPS 5004), 9 ft posts, uncompressed, 128x128 blocks. ELEVATIONS ARE IN FEET (metadata: altunits feet, NAVD88 via GEOID09) and are converted to metres on ingest; max 5873 in the raw grid is 1790 m, which is right for the Chugach/Talkeetna summits here and impossible in metres. Verified against matsu_2019 at Palmer airport, Sutton and Chickaloon: 70.78/137.04/414.87 m vs 70.94/137.17/415.10 m. Lies in UTM zone 6. max_zoom 15 (2.27 m) for 2.74 m source.

datasets.title: Seward 2023 bare-earth DTM
datasets.notes: Arrives as a valid COG (LZW, 512 blocks, overviews) in a COMPOUND CRS: NAD83(2011) / UTM 6N + NAVD88 height (GEOID12B), unit metre. Already the target zone, so the archive stage copies (same reasoning as kbay_2023). 75000x84000 grid, 38.8% valid: Resurrection Bay from Seward north up the Resurrection River valley. Source directory also holds _shade and _mod5 derivatives, which the viewer renders client-side instead.
